findings.issue: The Word-less PDF/preview does not mirror the template. I rendered the reference template through LetterComposer.RenderHtml (scratchpad probe against the built Wakeel.Reports.dll) and the printed sheet comes out as: the date/number block twice, the subject line twice, the signature block twice, the header letterhead («الترويسة») twice AND at the very bottom of the sheet after the signature, and all 18 of the template's padding blank paragraphs kept. Three separate causes: (a) LetterTemplateInspector.ReadParagraphs walks root.Descendants<Paragraph>(), which visits both the mc:Choice drawing copy and the mc:Fallback VML copy of every text box — the reference template has 6 AlternateContent blocks / 12 txbxContent, each pair carrying the same words (this is correct for Compose, which must fill both, and wrong for the renderer, which prints what it is given); (b) LetterOpenXml.TextParts yields the main part first and the header parts after it, so the letterhead lands under the signature; (c) LetterBodyWriter.TrimBlankParagraphsAfter has no counterpart in the renderer, so the closing phrase is pushed onto a second page. On a machine without Word this is the only PDF an approved official letter can produce.
findings.fix:
Give the renderer its own reader rather than reusing the composer's walk. In LetterTemplateInspector add an overload (or a new internal reader) that (i) skips any paragraph with a DocumentFormat.OpenXml.AlternateContentFallback ancestor, so each text box is read once, and (ii) returns the header parts' paragraphs before the main part's, tagged so LetterHtmlRenderer can emit them in a `
` block above the sheet's flow; leave LetterOpenXml.Paragraphs (used by Compose and by Check) exactly as it is. In LetterHtmlRenderer.Render, after the body has been written, collapse a run of consecutive blank template lines to one `

`. Add tests asserting that the number, the subject and the sender each occur exactly once in the rendering and that the letterhead line's index is lower than the body's.

findings.issue: IsPlainLetterPackage screens a template only on the way in (CheckAsync / SaveLocalCopyAsync). GetAsync — the method every letter is composed from — returns ReadLocalCopy() and ReadSetupCopyAsync() unscreened. The local copy is exactly the file IWordAutomation.EditFileAsync hands to Word for the office to edit and save over in place (TemplateService.LocalCopyPath, App.xaml.cs W88 path), so an office that attaches a template on a share, links a picture or embeds an object while editing turns that into the template in force; every letter then carries the external relationship and is opened by whichever office receives it, which is the exact thing the guard was written to stop. WordSession's AutomationSecurity=3 covers macros but does not stop Word following an attachedTemplate/linked-object relationship, and it protects only this machine, not the recipient's.
findings.fix: Run the same screen where the template is read, not only where it is written: in ReadLocalCopy return null when IsPlainLetterPackage(content) is false, and in ReadSetupCopyAsync do the same, so GetAsync falls through to the next source and ultimately to the built-in template. Add a test that a local copy carrying an external attachedTemplate relationship (PackageTamper already builds one) is ignored by GetAsync and that the returned LetterTemplateSource.Origin is BuiltIn.

findings.issue: TextOf reads only w:t nodes, so w:br and w:tab inside a paragraph vanish. The reference template's date/number text box is one paragraph holding two w:br (verified in word/document.xml), and the HTML rendering therefore prints «<bdi>19 صفر 1448</bdi><bdi>2 أغسطس 2026</bdi>رقم الصادر: …» as one run-together line — the two dates read as «14482» where they meet. Compose is unaffected (its index arithmetic is over text nodes only), but the fallback PDF shows a mangled date block.
findings.fix:
Leave TextOf as it is (the composer's splice depends on its indices) and give the HTML reader a separate join that maps Break to "\n" and TabChar to a space, then have LetterHtmlRenderer emit one `

` per resulting segment. Assert in LetterHtmlRendererTests that «19 صفر 1448» and «2 أغسطس 2026» are on different lines of the rendering.

findings.issue: A template paragraph that writes @نص المراسلة twice keeps the second mark in the finished letter: Fill inserts the body once per paragraph (deliberately, and correctly, to stop the letter being poured into its own words) but never removes the marks it did not use, so the printed letter and the PDF still show «@نص المراسلة». LetterHtmlRenderer has the same hole — it splits the line at the first occurrence and the suffix goes through Fill(), which has no entry for the body mark. The spec requires that no placeholder ever reaches the printed letter.
findings.fix: In LetterComposer.Fill, after LetterBodyWriter.Insert returns, splice every remaining occurrence of LetterMarks.Body out of the paragraph it wrote into (a small loop over LetterOpenXml.FindFirst with an empty replacement). In LetterHtmlRenderer.AppendBody, strip LetterMarks.Body from prefix and suffix before filling them. Add a test with a template line carrying the mark twice, asserting no '@' survives in either output.

elements: there is no letterhead area (the header part is emitted last, at the foot of the sheet) and no right/left blocks (the template floats the date/number box and the addressee on opposite sides; both are emitted inline in the flow, duplicated).
